messages:
nina: Anyone else hit weird overload-resolution when using the SDK in an edge worker? I have two overloads for `request` (one for streaming, one for single response) and tsc chooses the streaming signature and types the payload as `unknown` so downstream code is full of `as any` hacks.

leo: yup. That smells like an overload ordering / contextual typing issue + differences between TS's moduleResolution and the emitted d.ts. Can you paste the two overload signatures?

nina: Sure:```ts
request<T>(opts: { input: T; stream?: false }): Promise<Response<T>>;
request<T>(opts: { input: T; stream: true }): AsyncIterable<Chunk<T>>;
```
At callsite `client.request({ input: myInput })` ends up matching the stream overload and myInput becomes `unknown`.

sam: a few possible culprits: 1) the distributed d.ts might have non-generic overloads compiled down or with `any` on parameters; 2) tsserver can sometimes prefer the latter overload depending on `strictFunctionTypes` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` flags; 3) bundlers that rewrite call expressions can change contextual signatures.

olga: also check `skipLibCheck` and `skipDefaultLibCheck`. If the SDK shipped a merged declaration file where overloads are emitted in a different order, TS will pick the first applicable overload but inference can differ. Do you see the same when using plain node tsc (not the edge bundler)?

nina: running `tsc --noEmit` locally shows correct inference. The problem appears only after esbuild bundling for the edge deploy.

leo: esbuild can collapse overloads if you feed it a transpiled .d.ts path or if it resolves to a compiled JS-only entry without the `.d.ts` alongside. The edge project may be resolving to the SDK's runtime ESM file which lacks proper types at the export boundary.

sam: try a minimal repro: create a tiny project that `import type { Client } from '@redwood/inference';` and then `declare const c: Client; c.request({ input: 123 })` and run `tsc`. If that passes, the issue is in the bundler pipeline.

nina: repro shows tsc OK. Esbuild output (we compile to single file for Cloudflare) has this snippet in the bundle header where it rewrites exports:```js
var r={};exports.Client=r;
```
so types are removed at bundle time.

olga: that explains it. Two remediation paths: 1) treat the SDK as an external in the edge bundle so types are resolved at build time from node_modules (no code bundled), 2) ensure you preserve type-only imports via `--bundle` flags that keep `import type` and don't mangle runtime-only reexports, 3) ask SDK to provide a smaller `types` entry that points to a plain dts with correct overloads and generic markers.

sam: also try flipping `importsNotUsedAsValues` to `preserve` in tsconfig so type-only imports survive some transforms. For esbuild, there's often a config like `tsconfig: { importsNotUsedAsValues: 'preserve' }` that matters.

nina: I'm currently marking the SDK as external which works, but not ideal for our zero-disk edge build. Filed a tiny issue on infra: make esbuild externalize `@redwood/inference` for now.

leo: FYI `unknown` vs `any`: if inference fails because the compiler can't relate type parameters across overloads it will widen. If you explicitly annotate overloads on the SDK with constraint like `T extends object = any` it can help. We should request SDK emits overloads with clearer constraints.

olga: small tactical fix you can try: add an intermediate typed overload local to your app:```ts
declare module '@redwood/inference' {
  interface Client {
    request<T>(opts: { input: T; stream?: false }): Promise<Response<T>>;
  }
}
```
This merges into the module and can help TS pick the correct resolution. Ugly but works until SDK ships a fix.

nina: good tip. One more weirdness: VS Code's intellisense shows correct types after a reload, but compile still errors; so dev experience is split.

sam: that's tsserver vs tsc discrepancy — tsserver might use different resolution caches. Restarting tsserver or clearing the workspace cache sometimes aligns them. Add a CI check that runs `tsc --noEmit` after your bundle step to catch this before deploy.

devbot: Created infra task #789: "esbuild: externalize @redwood/inference for edge workers until SDK types are stabilized" - https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-789

nina: thanks all. Will externalize for now and ping SDK with a request to avoid overload-ordering/regression in emitted d.ts. Also adding a small compile-only test in our repo to catch this next time. :sparkles:
